Krusader 2.5.0 answers three points raised in the Unraid support thread: a closed window comes back, there is a diff viewer, and the memory the container uses is now a setting instead of a fact.

## ✨ Added

- **Kompare is bundled.** *File → Compare by Content…* opens two selected files in a side-by-side diff. Until now that menu entry only replied that Krusader could not find any of the supported diff frontends. Nothing to set up: Krusader finds Kompare on its own and remembers where it is.
- **A screen-size dropdown with the cost written on it.** `MAX_RES` lists sizes from 1080p up to the full 15360x8640, each entry labelled with the memory it needs, so the trade is visible while you choose rather than buried in a wiki page.
- **A free field for anything not in the list.** `MAX_RES_CUSTOM` takes any `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, for example `3440x1440` or `6016x3384`, and wins over the dropdown when you fill it in. Two fields rather than one editable dropdown, because Unraid renders any variable with preset values as a plain select with no way to type into it.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The screen size is where the container's memory goes, and now you can see it.** The X server reserves its whole framebuffer up front, roughly four bytes per pixel, no matter how large your browser window is. At the full size that is 530 MB before anything else runs, which is why this image looked heavy next to the noVNC ones. Nothing is capped unless you ask for it: the container idles around 700 MB at the full size, about 295 MB at 4K, 210 MB at 3440x1440 and 200 MB at 1080p. All measured on a live container with a client connected.
- **A typo cannot take the desktop down.** The screen size goes straight to the X server as a command line argument, so `1920*1080` would have stopped it from starting and left you with no desktop and no hint why. Such a value is now ignored with a line in the container log, and the next usable setting applies. That covers sizes that merely look plausible too: `15360x86400` would ask for a five gigabyte framebuffer and be killed on every boot, so each side is bounded at 16384, which sits above the largest preset.
- **The Shift-on-function-keys patch is gone, because the base image now carries the fix.** This image shipped a small bridge patch so that Shift+F4 kept its Shift. Upstream solved the same thing one layer up and more broadly, so Shift+Home and Shift+Arrow keep their Shift too. The patch was built to stop the build the day the base caught up, and that is what it did.
- **The session and screen-size scripts have tests now.** They run the real scripts against a stub Krusader and pin the behaviour below: restart after a quit, no restart after a container stop, the quit-before-signal order, both spin guards, and which screen size wins. They run in CI on every push.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Quitting Krusader no longer leaves a black screen.** Closing the application in the browser (*File → Quit*, `Ctrl+Q` or the window's X) ended the session and left an empty desktop behind, and only a container restart brought Krusader back. It now starts again on its own, so refreshing the browser tab is enough.
- **Stopping the container still keeps your settings.** The session asks Krusader to quit itself before the container goes down, and that request no longer depends on a process ID a badly timed signal could invalidate. Window geometry and the status-bar state survive a stop exactly as before, since Krusader writes that state as it goes.
- **A Krusader that cannot start stops instead of spinning.** Five failed starts in a row, or twenty instant exits of any kind, and the session gives up and logs why. Before, a program that died immediately on every attempt would have been restarted forever.
- **A rejected screen size can no longer reach the X server anyway.** Docker environment variables are imported into the service environment before any of this runs, so an unusable value was sitting there already and would have been used despite the fallback. It is now removed, which is what makes the fallback real.
